introduction:
Introduction About MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET

MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET contains Sodium Aminosalicylate which belongs to the group of medicines called Antitubercular agents. It is used to manage tuberculosis that cannot be controlled by other medicines.

Tuberculosis is a serious bacterial infection caused by a bacterium called Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It is characterized by persistent cough with mucus, blood-stained phlegm, shortness of breath, weight loss, fever, extreme tiredness, stomach pain, headache and fits.

Take MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET for the stipulated duration instructed by your doctor even if you feel better during the midway of the therapy to achieve better results. Failing to complete the full course of the therapy or skipping doses in between the therapy may not result in adequate infection control.

Before taking MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney, or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have HIV infection, stomach ulcer, thyroid problems or high blood pressure.

MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET should be used in pregnant women only if it is considered necessary by the physician. It is generally not recommended for use in breastfeeding women. However, consult your doctor for advice.

During management with MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET, your doctor will closely monitor your liver functions and thyroid functions to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

The most common side effects of taking MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET are nausea, vomiting, giddiness, stomach pain, bloating and skin rashes. Inform your doctor if they trouble you.
uses: Manage resistant tuberculosis when other medicines are not effective
usesDetails:
Uses Of MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET
Manage resistant tuberculosis when other medicines are not effective
mechanismOfAction:
How MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET Works

MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET is a bacteriostatic agent. It works by blocking the production of an important vitamin called folic acid in the bacterial cell which is required for its survival. It also limits the uptake of iron by the bacterial cell that is required for its growth and multiplication. Collectively, these actions kill the susceptible bacteria, manage their further growth and multiplication and reduce the severity of the infection.
usageDetails:
How to use MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET

Take MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. It can be taken with or without food.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and severity of the infection.

Do not stop taking MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET once your symptoms subside. It is important to take MONOPAS 1000MG TABLET for the stipulated duration recommended by your doctor to achieve better results.

MYCOCOX TABLET is a combination of Isoniazid and Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antitubercular agents. It is used to manage tuberculosis and bacterial infection of membranes covering the brain, and spinal cord. It is also used to manage contagious disease of skin, nerves, mucous membrane, and other conditions in affected individuals.

MYCOCOX TABLET is not recommended for use in patients allergic to Isoniazid, and/or Rifampicin. Before taking MYCOCOX TABLET, inform your doctor if you are scheduled for any upcoming surgery, and/or suffering from pre-existing diseases, liver problems (such as cirrhosis of liver)/kidney problems (such as renal insufficiency).

MYCOCOX TABLET should be used with caution during pregnancy and in women planning for pregnancy. It is also advised to be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it may pass through breast milk.

MYCOCOX TABLET should be used with caution in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) and is advised to be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65years and above) after consulting the doctor. 

The most common side effects of taking MYCOCOX TABLET are hypersensitivity reaction (associated with signs such as skin rash, red itchy welt, and/or shortness of breath), loss of vision/hearing, flu-like syndrome, and/or arthralgia (joint stiffness). Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsens.

introduction:
Introduction About CADIRIFA TABLET

CADIRIFA TABLET is a combination of Isoniazid and Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antitubercular agents. It is used to manage tuberculosis and bacterial infection of membranes covering the brain, and spinal cord. It is also used to manage contagious disease of skin, nerves, mucous membrane, and other conditions in affected individuals.

CADIRIFA TABLET is not recommended for use in patients allergic to Isoniazid, and/or Rifampicin. Before taking CADIRIFA TABLET, inform your doctor if you are scheduled for any upcoming surgery, and/or suffering from pre-existing diseases, liver problems (such as cirrhosis of liver)/kidney problems (such as renal insufficiency).

CADIRIFA TABLET should be used with caution during pregnancy and in women planning for pregnancy. It is also advised to be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it may pass through breast milk.

CADIRIFA TABLET should be used with caution in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) and is advised to be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65years and above) after consulting the doctor. 

The most common side effects of taking CADIRIFA TABLET are hypersensitivity reaction (associated with signs such as skin rash, red itchy welt, and/or shortness of breath), loss of vision/hearing, flu-like syndrome, and/or arthralgia (joint stiffness). Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsens.

introduction:
Introduction About MACOX 450MG CAPSULE

MACOX 450MG CAPSULE contains Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antibacterial. It is used to manage bacterial infections such as tuberculosis (affects the lungs), legionnaires disease (lung inflammation), brucellosis (infection spreading from animal to person), leprosy (causes skin lesions and nerve damage) and serious staphylococcal infections.

It also manages the infections caused by Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitides (who are the carriers but do not show the symptoms), thereby managing and managing the onset of flu and meningitis. The doctor may ask you to take blood tests and liver function tests before starting management with MACOX 450MG CAPSULE. MACOX 450MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you have yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice).

Before taking MACOX 450MG CAPSULE, it is recommended to inform your doctor if you have liver, kidney problems, diabetes, are underweight or malnourished, have a rare blood problem (porphyria), bleeding or a tendency to bruise easily. Also, inform your doctor if symptoms of tuberculosis return or get worse, are wearing contact lenses, are vitamin K deficient or have hypoprothrombinemia (deficient clotting factor).

MACOX 450MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant and breastfeeding women. MACOX 450MG CAPSULE should be used with caution in children under 2 years of age and in elderly patients above 65 years of age. The most common side effects seen are nausea, vomiting, chills, fever. Consult your doctor if symptoms do not improve.
uses: Infections caused by Haemophilus influenzae (causes flu) and Neisseria meningitides (causes meningitis)

MACOX 450MG CAPSULE works by managing protein synthesis and interferes with the enzymes present in the bacteria causing its death. This results in a reduction in the count of infection-causing bacteria, thereby managing bacterial infections.

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug Interactions:

Before taking MACOX 450MG CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicine:

Medicines used to manage HIV infection (Ex. saquinavir, ritonavir)
Medicines used to manage indigestion such as antacids (Ex. aluminium hydroxide, magnesium carbonate)
Other medicines used to manage tuberculosis (Ex. P-Aminosalicylic Acid)
Medicines used to thin the blood (Ex. clopidrogel, warfarrin)
Medicines used to lower cholesterol (Ex. atorvastatin, rosuvastatin)
Medicines for heart problems or to control your heartbeat (Ex. atenolol, bisprolol), lower the blood pressure (Ex. diuretics like eplerenone)
Medicines used to manage thought disorders (Ex. antipsychotics like haloperidol), reduce anxiety (Ex. hypnotics-lorazepam), to induce sleep (Ex. barbiturates-phenobarbital), manage depression (Ex. amitriptyline)
Medicines used to manage epilepsy (Ex. phenytoin), disease of motor neurons (Ex. riluzole)
Medicines used to manage various viral infections (Ex. indinavir, telaprevir, amprenavir, nelfinavir, atazanavir, lopinavir, neviparine, daclatasvir, simeprevir, sofosbuvir and telaprevir)
Medicines used to manage fungal diseases (Ex. ketoconazole, clotrimazole), bacterial infections (Ex. amoxicillin, cephalosporin), tapeworm infections (Ex. praziquantel)
Medicines used to lower the immune system response (Ex. ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus)
Medicines used to manage pneumonia (Ex. atovaquone)
Medicines used for contraception (Ex. estrogen, progestogens)
Medicines used to manage cancer (Ex. imatinib, irinotecan, ethinyloestradiol, levonorgestrel or dydrogesterone), for breast cancer or endometriosis (Ex. tamoxifen, gestrinone, toremifene)
Medicines used to manage thyroid gland problems (Ex. levothyroxine)
Medicines used to manage gout and other pains (Ex. aspirin, etoricoxib, codeine, morphine, fentanyl, pethidine, etoricoxib, aspirin and indomethacin)
Medicines used to manage inflammation in the body such as corticosteroids (Ex. hydrocortisone, betamethasone and prednisolone)
Medicines used during withdrawal from heroin (Ex. methadone)
Medicines used to manage diabetes (Ex. metformin)
Medicines used before surgery to relax the mind and body (Ex. halothane)
Medicines used for nausea (Ex. ondansetron, aprepitant)
Medicines used for malaria (Ex. quinine)
Medicines used to manage difficulty breathing and wheezing sound (Ex. theophylline)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took too much of MACOX 450MG CAPSULE, visit the nearby hospital or consult your doctor immediately. Signs and symptoms of overdosage are feeling sick (nausea) along with vomiting and pain in abdomen, increased itch (pruritus), headache and increased lethargy, feeling of drowsiness, swelling of the face, eyes or eyelids, fast or uneven heartbeat, dizziness, fits and heart attack.

name: VICOX ZE Tablet 6's
introduction:
Introduction About VICOX ZE TABLET

VICOX ZE TABLET is a combination of Ethambutol, Isoniazid and Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antituberculosis agents respectively. It is used for the initial management of tuberculosis. Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection which spreads through inhaling tiny droplets from the coughs or sneezes of an infected person. Symptoms such as persistent cough with sputum and blood, weight loss, night sweats, high temperature, tiredness and fatigue, loss of appetite and swelling in the neck.

Your doctor will perform some regular blood tests such as liver function test, visual acuity, uric acid level to monitor any changes in your body. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may cause liver damage. VICOX ZE TABLET is not recommended in patients with acute liver disease, drug-induced liver disease, inflammation of the optic nerve (optic neuritis) and body weight of less than 20 kg. VICOX ZE TABLET should be used with caution in patients with hepatitis and kidney disease, suffer from tingling in the hands and feet (peripheral neuropathy), HIV infection, hypersensitive to ethionamide or niacin (nicotinic acid), epilepsy or a history of psychiatric disease and diabetes or porphyria.

VICOX ZE TABLET should be used with caution in pregnant and breastfeeding women. Contact your doctor before taking VICOX ZE TABLET. The most common side effects of taking VICOX ZE TABLET are peripheral neuropathy (sensations of tingling, pricking, or numbness of the skin, especially in the feet and hands), increased liver enzymes & uric acid levels in blood, flushing, reddish discoloration of body fluids such as urine, sputum, tears, saliva and sweat, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea, and vomiting or skin reactions. Consult your physician if you experience any of the above side effects worsen.
usesDetails:
Uses Of VICOX ZE TABLET
Used to manage tuberculosis
mechanismOfAction:
How VICOX ZE TABLET Works

VICOX ZE TABLET helps to manage tuberculosis, where Ethambutol has bacteriostatic properties that inhibits cell wall synthesis. Isoniazid destroys and manages the growth of bacteria. Rifampicin acts via the inhibition of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, leading to a suppression of RNA synthesis and cell death.
usageDetails:
How to use VICOX ZE TABLET

Take VICOX ZE TABLET as advised by your physician. Take the medicine, with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the right dose depends on your age, body weight and severity of infection.

introduction:
Introduction About RCIN 100MG SYRUP

RCIN 100MG SYRUP contains Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antibacterial. It is used in the management of serious bacterial infections such as tuberculosis (affects the lungs), legionnaires disease (lung inflammation), brucellosis (infection spreading from animal to people), leprosy (causes skin lesions and nerve damage) along with other medicines and also manages haemophilus influenzae.

It is also used to stop meningitis (inflammation of the membranes and fluid surrounding the brain and spinal cord) and haemophilus influenzae (in children aged 4 years or younger). Your doctor may ask you to take blood tests and liver function tests before the management with RCIN 100MG SYRUP. RCIN 100MG SYRUP is not recommended for use if you have yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice).

Before taking RCIN 100MG SYRUP, it is recommended to inform your doctor if you have liver, kidney problems, diabetes, feel numb or weak in your arms and legs (peripheral neuropathy), are underweight or malnourished. Also, inform your doctor if you have a rare blood problem (porphyria), bleeding or a tendency to bruise easily, symptoms of tuberculosis return/get worse or are wearing contact lenses.

RCIN 100MG SYRUP should be used with caution in pregnant women. It is not recommended for use in breastfeeding women. RCIN 100MG SYRUP should be used with caution in children under 2 years of age and elderly patients above 65 years of age. The most common side effects seen are nausea, vomiting, chills, fever. Consult your doctor if symptoms do not improve.

RCIN 100MG SYRUP must be taken with caution if you are diagnosed with liver disease. Consult your doctor before taking RCIN 100MG SYRUP.
Do not take RCIN 100MG SYRUP if you are allergic to Rifampicin and/or any other constituents present in the medicine.

Others

RCIN 100MG SYRUP is not recommended for use if you:

Have yellowish tinge to eyes and skin which may be indicative of jaundice 

Before taking RCIN 100MG SYRUP, inform your doctor if you:

Have diabetes (elevated level of sugar in blood)
Have peripheral neuropathy which is characterized by feeling of weakness and numbness in feet and hands
Are underweight and/or malnourished
Are diagnosed with a blood disorder called Porphyria characterized by the appearance of purple colored rash on skin.
Are prone to bleeding and/or bruising easily
Wear contact lens
Notice worsening and/or return of your initial symptoms of tuberculosis

Use in Pediatrics:
RCIN 100MG SYRUP must be taken in caution in children below 2 years of age. Consult your doctor before taking it as they can decide the correct and required dosage, frequency and strength of RCIN 100MG SYRUP based on age, disease condition and body weight of the child.

Use in Geriatrics:
RCIN 100MG SYRUP must be taken with caution in elderly patients (above the age of 65 years). Consult your doctor before taking RCIN 100MG SYRUP.

A. Drug-Drug Interactions:

Before taking RCIN 100MG SYRUP, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicine:

Medicines used to manage HIV infection (Ex. saquinavir, ritonavir)
Medicines used to manage indigestion such as antacids (Ex. aluminium hydroxide, magnesium carbonate)
Other medicines used to manage tuberculosis (Ex. P-Aminosalicylic Acid)
Medicines used to thin the blood (Ex. clopidrogel, warfarrin)
Medicines used to lower cholesterol (Ex. atorvastatin, rosuvastatin)
Medicines for heart problems or to control your heartbeat (Ex. atenolol, bisprolol), lower the blood pressure (Ex. diuretics like eplerenone)
Medicines used to manage thought disorders (Ex. antipsychotics like haloperidol), reduce anxiety (Ex. hypnotics-lorazepam), to induce sleep (Ex. barbiturates-phenobarbital), manage depression (Ex. amitriptyline)
Medicines used to manage epilepsy (Ex. phenytoin), disease of motor neurons (Ex. riluzole)
Medicines used to manage various viral infections (Ex. indinavir, telaprevir, amprenavir, nelfinavir, atazanavir, lopinavir, neviparine, daclatasvir, simeprevir, sofosbuvir and telaprevir)
Medicines used to manage fungal diseases (Ex. ketoconazole, clotrimazole), bacterial infections (Ex. amoxicillin, cephalosporin), tapeworm infections (Ex. praziquantel)
Medicines used to lower the immune system response (Ex. ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus)
Medicines used to manage pneumonia (Ex. atovaquone)
Medicines used for contraception (Ex. estrogen, progestogens)
Medicines used to manage cancer (Ex. imatinib, irinotecan, ethinyloestradiol, levonorgestrel or dydrogesterone), for breast cancer or endometriosis (Ex. tamoxifen, gestrinone, toremifene)
Medicines used to manage thyroid gland problems (Ex. levothyroxine)
Medicines used to manage gout and other pains (Ex. aspirin, etoricoxib, codeine, morphine, fentanyl, pethidine, etoricoxib, aspirin and indomethacin)
Medicines used to manage inflammation in the body such as corticosteroids (Ex. hydrocortisone, betamethasone and prednisolone)
Medicines used during withdrawal from heroin (Ex. methadone)
Medicines used to manage diabetes (Ex. metformin) 
Medicines used before surgery to relax the mind and body (Ex. halothane)
Medicines used for nausea (Ex. ondansetron, aprepitant)
Medicines used for malaria (Ex. quinine)
Medicines used to manage difficulty breathing and wheezing sound (Ex. theophylline)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took more of RCIN 100MG SYRUP, visit the nearby hospital or consult your doctor immediately. The symptoms of overdosage are nausea, vomiting, stomachache, itch and headache. The patient may also experience tiredness, sleepiness and dizziness, along with swelling of face and eyes, difficult breathing and fast, uneven heartbeat, heart attack and fits.

introduction:
Introduction About AKT 3 COMBIPACK

AKT 3 COMBIPACK is a combination of Ethambutol, Isoniazid and Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antituberculosis agents respectively. It is used for the initial management of tuberculosis. Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection which spreads through inhaling tiny droplets from the coughs or sneezes of an infected person. Symptoms such as persistent cough with sputum and blood, weight loss, night sweats, high temperature, tiredness and fatigue, loss of appetite and swelling in the neck.

Your doctor will perform some regular blood tests such as liver function test, visual acuity, uric acid level to monitor any changes in your body. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may cause liver damage. AKT 3 COMBIPACK is not recommended in patients with acute liver disease, drug-induced liver disease, inflammation of the optic nerve (optic neuritis) and body weight of less than 20 kg. AKT 3 COMBIPACK should be used with caution in patients with hepatitis and kidney disease, suffer from tingling in the hands and feet (peripheral neuropathy), HIV infection, hypersensitive to ethionamide or niacin (nicotinic acid), epilepsy or a history of psychiatric disease and diabetes or porphyria.

AKT 3 COMBIPACK should be used with caution in pregnant and breastfeeding women. Contact your doctor before taking AKT 3 COMBIPACK. The most common side effects of taking AKT 3 COMBIPACK are peripheral neuropathy (sensations of tingling, pricking, or numbness of the skin, especially in the feet and hands), increased liver enzymes & uric acid levels in blood, flushing, reddish discoloration of body fluids such as urine, sputum, tears, saliva and sweat, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea, and vomiting or skin reactions. Consult your physician if you experience any of the above side effects worsen.
usesDetails:
Uses Of AKT 3 COMBIPACK
Used to manage tuberculosis
mechanismOfAction:
How AKT 3 COMBIPACK Works

AKT 3 COMBIPACK helps to manage tuberculosis, where Ethambutol has bacteriostatic properties that inhibits cell wall synthesis. Isoniazid destroys and manages the growth of bacteria. Rifampicin acts via the inhibition of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, leading to a suppression of RNA synthesis and cell death.
usageDetails:
How to use AKT 3 COMBIPACK

Take AKT 3 COMBIPACK as advised by your physician. Take the medicine, with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the right dose depends on your age, body weight and severity of infection.

introduction:
Introduction About RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET

RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET is a combination of Ethambutol, Isoniazid and Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antituberculosis agents respectively. It is used for the initial management of tuberculosis. Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection which spreads through inhaling tiny droplets from the coughs or sneezes of an infected person. Symptoms such as persistent cough with sputum and blood, weight loss, night sweats, high temperature, tiredness and fatigue, loss of appetite and swelling in the neck.

Your doctor will perform some regular blood tests such as liver function test, visual acuity, uric acid level to monitor any changes in your body. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may cause liver damage. RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET is not recommended in patients with acute liver disease, drug-induced liver disease, inflammation of the optic nerve (optic neuritis) and body weight of less than 20 kg. RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with hepatitis and kidney disease, suffer from tingling in the hands and feet (peripheral neuropathy), HIV infection, hypersensitive to ethionamide or niacin (nicotinic acid), epilepsy or a history of psychiatric disease and diabetes or porphyria.

RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET should be used with caution in pregnant and breastfeeding women. Contact your doctor before taking RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET. The most common side effects of taking RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET are peripheral neuropathy (sensations of tingling, pricking, or numbness of the skin, especially in the feet and hands), increased liver enzymes & uric acid levels in blood, flushing, reddish discoloration of body fluids such as urine, sputum, tears, saliva and sweat, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea, and vomiting or skin reactions. Consult your physician if you experience any of the above side effects worsen.

Used to manage tuberculosis
mechanismOfAction:
How RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET Works

RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET helps to manage tuberculosis, where Ethambutol has bacteriostatic properties that inhibits cell wall synthesis. Isoniazid destroys and manages the growth of bacteria. Rifampicin acts via the inhibition of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, leading to a suppression of RNA synthesis and cell death.

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Antibiotics such as voriconazole, clarithromycin (medicine used to manage fungal infections) 
HIV protease inhibitors (Ex. efavirenz, nevirapine) (drugs used to manage HIV infection)
Aluminium hydroxide (medicine used to manage diseases related to the gastric acid)
Disulfiram (medicine used for the management of chronic alcoholism)
Medicines to manage fungal infections (Ex. ketoconazole, fluconazole)
Quinine (medicine used to manage malaria)
Immunosuppressant drugs (Ex. cyclosporine, tacrolimus)
Medicines to manage heart conditions (Ex. verapamil, digoxin)
Medicines to manage blood lipids (Ex. simvastatin)
Medicines to manage diabetes (Ex. glibenclamide)
Oral contraceptive pills (medicines used to manage unwanted pregnancy)
Medicines to manage epileptic seizures (Ex. phenytoin, carbamazepine, valproate)
Medicines used to help you sleep (Ex. diazepam, flurazepam, triazolam, midazolam)
Medicines for the management of certain psychiatric conditions (Ex. chlorpromazine, haloperidol)
Medicines for management of blood clots (Ex. warfarin)
Medicines used at surgery (Ex. alfentanil, enflurane)
Corticosteroids (Ex. prednisolone, medicines for the management of inflammations and other diseases, such as asthma or rheumatoid arthritis)
Paracetamol (used for pain)

B. Drug-Food interaction:

When taken with cheese or fish, RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET may cause redness, itching of the skin, hot feeling, rapid or pounding heartbeat, sweating, chills or clammy feeling, headache, and/or light-headedness.

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally takes too much of RIMTHREE FDC 150/275 TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Symptoms of overdose may develop vomiting, gastrointestinal disturbances, fever, headache, dizziness, slurring of speech, hallucinations and/or visual disturbances.

name: ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE 4'S
introduction:
Introduction About ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE

ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE is a combination of Isoniazid and Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antitubercular agents. It is used to manage tuberculosis and bacterial infection of membranes covering the brain, and spinal cord. It is also used to manage contagious disease of skin, nerves, mucous membrane, and other conditions in affected individuals.

ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients allergic to Isoniazid, and/or Rifampicin. Before taking ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you are scheduled for any upcoming surgery, and/or suffering from pre-existing diseases, liver problems (such as cirrhosis of liver)/kidney problems (such as renal insufficiency).

ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE should be used with caution during pregnancy and in women planning for pregnancy. It is also advised to be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it may pass through breast milk.

ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE should be used with caution in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) and is advised to be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65years and above) after consulting the doctor. 

The most common side effects of taking ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE are hypersensitivity reaction (associated with signs such as skin rash, red itchy welt, and/or shortness of breath), loss of vision/hearing, flu-like syndrome, and/or arthralgia (joint stiffness). Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsens.

name: WOKEX 3 Kit 1's
introduction:
Introduction About WOKEX 3 KIT

WOKEX 3 KIT is a combination of Ethambutol, Isoniazid and Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antituberculosis agents respectively. It is used for the initial management of tuberculosis. Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection which spreads through inhaling tiny droplets from the coughs or sneezes of an infected person. Symptoms such as persistent cough with sputum and blood, weight loss, night sweats, high temperature, tiredness and fatigue, loss of appetite and swelling in the neck.

Your doctor will perform some regular blood tests such as liver function test, visual acuity, uric acid level to monitor any changes in your body. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may cause liver damage. WOKEX 3 KIT is not recommended in patients with acute liver disease, drug-induced liver disease, inflammation of the optic nerve (optic neuritis) and body weight of less than 20 kg. WOKEX 3 KIT should be used with caution in patients with hepatitis and kidney disease, suffer from tingling in the hands and feet (peripheral neuropathy), HIV infection, hypersensitive to ethionamide or niacin (nicotinic acid), epilepsy or a history of psychiatric disease and diabetes or porphyria.

WOKEX 3 KIT should be used with caution in pregnant and breastfeeding women. Contact your doctor before taking WOKEX 3 KIT. The most common side effects of taking WOKEX 3 KIT are peripheral neuropathy (sensations of tingling, pricking, or numbness of the skin, especially in the feet and hands), increased liver enzymes & uric acid levels in blood, flushing, reddish discoloration of body fluids such as urine, sputum, tears, saliva and sweat, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea, and vomiting or skin reactions. Consult your physician if you experience any of the above side effects worsen.
usesDetails:
Uses Of WOKEX 3 KIT
Used to manage tuberculosis
mechanismOfAction:
How WOKEX 3 KIT Works

WOKEX 3 KIT helps to manage tuberculosis, where Ethambutol has bacteriostatic properties that inhibits cell wall synthesis. Isoniazid destroys and manages the growth of bacteria. Rifampicin acts via the inhibition of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, leading to a suppression of RNA synthesis and cell death.
usageDetails:
How to use WOKEX 3 KIT

Take WOKEX 3 KIT as advised by your physician. Take the medicine, with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the right dose depends on your age, body weight and severity of infection.

name: RCIN 100MG SUSPENSION 60ML
introduction:
Introduction About RCIN 100MG SUSPENSION

RCIN 100MG SUSPENSION contains Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antibacterial. It is used in the management of serious bacterial infections such as tuberculosis (affects the lungs), legionnaires disease (lung inflammation), brucellosis (infection spreading from animal to people), leprosy (causes skin lesions and nerve damage) along with other medicines and also manages haemophilus influenzae.

It is also used to stop meningitis (inflammation of the membranes and fluid surrounding the brain and spinal cord) and haemophilus influenzae (in children aged 4 years or younger). Your doctor may ask you to take blood tests and liver function tests before the management with RCIN 100MG SUSPENSION. RCIN 100MG SUSPENSION is not recommended for use if you have yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice).

Before taking RCIN 100MG SUSPENSION, it is recommended to inform your doctor if you have liver, kidney problems, diabetes, feel numb or weak in your arms and legs (peripheral neuropathy), are underweight or malnourished. Also, inform your doctor if you have a rare blood problem (porphyria), bleeding or a tendency to bruise easily, symptoms of tuberculosis return/get worse or are wearing contact lenses.

RCIN 100MG SUSPENSION should be used with caution in pregnant women. It is not recommended for use in breastfeeding women. RCIN 100MG SUSPENSION should be used with caution in children under 2 years of age and elderly patients above 65 years of age. The most common side effects seen are nausea, vomiting, chills, fever. Consult your doctor if symptoms do not improve.

RCIN 100MG SUSPENSION is not recommended for use if you:

Have yellowish tinge to eyes and skin which may be indicative of jaundice

Have diabetes (elevated level of sugar in blood)
Have peripheral neuropathy which is characterized by feeling of weakness and numbness in feet and hands
Are underweight and/or malnourished
Are diagnosed with a blood disorder called Porphyria characterized by the appearance of purple colored rash on skin.
Are prone to bleeding and/or bruising easily
Wear contact lens
Notice worsening and/or return of your initial symptoms of tuberculosis

Use in Geriatrics:
RCIN 100MG SUSPENSION must be taken with caution in elderly patients (above the age of 65 years). Consult your doctor before taking RCIN 100MG SUSPENSION.

introduction:
Introduction About MACOX PLUS 450/300MG TABLET

MACOX PLUS 450/300MG TABLET is a combination of Isoniazid and Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antitubercular agents. It is used to manage tuberculosis and bacterial infection of membranes covering the brain, and spinal cord. It is also used to manage contagious disease of skin, nerves, mucous membrane, and other conditions in affected individuals.

MACOX PLUS 450/300MG TABLET is not recommended for use in patients allergic to Isoniazid, and/or Rifampicin. Before taking MACOX PLUS 450/300MG TABLET, inform your doctor if you are scheduled for any upcoming surgery, and/or suffering from pre-existing diseases, liver problems (such as cirrhosis of liver)/kidney problems (such as renal insufficiency).

MACOX PLUS 450/300MG TABLET should be used with caution during pregnancy and in women planning for pregnancy. It is also advised to be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it may pass through breast milk.

MACOX PLUS 450/300MG TABLET should be used with caution in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) and is advised to be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65years and above) after consulting the doctor. 

The most common side effects of taking MACOX PLUS 450/300MG TABLET are hypersensitivity reaction (associated with signs such as skin rash, red itchy welt, and/or shortness of breath), loss of vision/hearing, flu-like syndrome, and/or arthralgia (joint stiffness). Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsens.

introduction:
Introduction About LS RIF 450MG CAPSULE

LS RIF 450MG CAPSULE contains Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antibacterial. It is used to manage bacterial infections such as tuberculosis (affects the lungs), legionnaires disease (lung inflammation), brucellosis (infection spreading from animal to person), leprosy (causes skin lesions and nerve damage) and serious staphylococcal infections.

It also manages the infections caused by Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitides (who are the carriers but do not show the symptoms), thereby managing and managing the onset of flu and meningitis. The doctor may ask you to take blood tests and liver function tests before starting management with LS RIF 450MG CAPSULE. LS RIF 450MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you have yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice).

Before taking LS RIF 450MG CAPSULE, it is recommended to inform your doctor if you have liver, kidney problems, diabetes, are underweight or malnourished, have a rare blood problem (porphyria), bleeding or a tendency to bruise easily. Also, inform your doctor if symptoms of tuberculosis return or get worse, are wearing contact lenses, are vitamin K deficient or have hypoprothrombinemia (deficient clotting factor).

LS RIF 450MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant and breastfeeding women. LS RIF 450MG CAPSULE should be used with caution in children under 2 years of age and in elderly patients above 65 years of age. The most common side effects seen are nausea, vomiting, chills, fever. Consult your doctor if symptoms do not improve.

introduction:
Introduction About RHE KIT

RHE KIT is a combination of Ethambutol, Isoniazid and Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antituberculosis agents respectively. It is used for the initial management of tuberculosis. Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection which spreads through inhaling tiny droplets from the coughs or sneezes of an infected person. Symptoms such as persistent cough with sputum and blood, weight loss, night sweats, high temperature, tiredness and fatigue, loss of appetite and swelling in the neck.

Your doctor will perform some regular blood tests such as liver function test, visual acuity, uric acid level to monitor any changes in your body. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may cause liver damage. RHE KIT is not recommended in patients with acute liver disease, drug-induced liver disease, inflammation of the optic nerve (optic neuritis) and body weight of less than 20 kg. RHE KIT should be used with caution in patients with hepatitis and kidney disease, suffer from tingling in the hands and feet (peripheral neuropathy), HIV infection, hypersensitive to ethionamide or niacin (nicotinic acid), epilepsy or a history of psychiatric disease and diabetes or porphyria.

RHE KIT should be used with caution in pregnant and breastfeeding women. Contact your doctor before taking RHE KIT. The most common side effects of taking RHE KIT are peripheral neuropathy (sensations of tingling, pricking, or numbness of the skin, especially in the feet and hands), increased liver enzymes & uric acid levels in blood, flushing, reddish discoloration of body fluids such as urine, sputum, tears, saliva and sweat, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea, and vomiting or skin reactions. Consult your physician if you experience any of the above side effects worsen.
usesDetails:

Used to manage tuberculosis
mechanismOfAction:
How RHE KIT Works

RHE KIT helps to manage tuberculosis, where Ethambutol has bacteriostatic properties that inhibits cell wall synthesis. Isoniazid destroys and manages the growth of bacteria. Rifampicin acts via the inhibition of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, leading to a suppression of RNA synthesis and cell death.

Take RHE KIT as advised by your physician. Take the medicine, with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the right dose depends on your age, body weight and severity of infection.

introduction:
Introduction About RCIN SUSPENSION

RCIN SUSPENSION contains Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antibacterial. It is used in the management of serious bacterial infections such as tuberculosis (affects the lungs), legionnaires disease (lung inflammation), brucellosis (infection spreading from animal to people), leprosy (causes skin lesions and nerve damage) along with other medicines and also manages haemophilus influenzae.

It is also used to stop meningitis (inflammation of the membranes and fluid surrounding the brain and spinal cord) and haemophilus influenzae (in children aged 4 years or younger). Your doctor may ask you to take blood tests and liver function tests before the management with RCIN SUSPENSION. RCIN SUSPENSION is not recommended for use if you have yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice).

Before taking RCIN SUSPENSION, it is recommended to inform your doctor if you have liver, kidney problems, diabetes, feel numb or weak in your arms and legs (peripheral neuropathy), are underweight or malnourished. Also, inform your doctor if you have a rare blood problem (porphyria), bleeding or a tendency to bruise easily, symptoms of tuberculosis return/get worse or are wearing contact lenses.

RCIN SUSPENSION should be used with caution in pregnant women. It is not recommended for use in breastfeeding women. RCIN SUSPENSION should be used with caution in children under 2 years of age and elderly patients above 65 years of age. The most common side effects seen are nausea, vomiting, chills, fever. Consult your doctor if symptoms do not improve.

mechanismOfAction:
How RCIN SUSPENSION Works

RCIN SUSPENSION works by managing protein synthesis and interferes with the enzymes present in the bacteria causing its death. This results in the reduction in the count of infection-causing bacteria, thereby managing bacterial infections.
usageDetails:
How to use RCIN SUSPENSION

Take RCIN SUSPENSION as advised by your physician. Shake well before use. It is recommended to take RCIN SUSPENSION on an empty stomach. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you depending on your age, body weight and severity of infection.

warnings.details: RCIN SUSPENSION must be used with caution in women who are pregnant and/or planning pregnancy. Also, RCIN SUSPENSION may result in the ineffectiveness of oral contraception, hence using physical methods of contraception like condoms and coils are recommended. Always consult your doctor before taking RCIN SUSPENSION.
RCIN SUSPENSION is not recommended to be taken by nursing women since it may pass to the baby through mother’s milk. Consult your doctor before taking RCIN SUSPENSION.
Do not drive and use heavy machinery after taking RCIN SUSPENSION as it might make you feel dizzy, faint and can adversely affect the vision. Consult your doctor before taking RCIN SUSPENSION.
RCIN SUSPENSION must be taken with caution if you are diagnosed with any kidney disease. Consult your doctor before taking RCIN SUSPENSION.
RCIN SUSPENSION must be taken with caution if you are diagnosed with liver disease. Consult your doctor before taking RCIN SUSPENSION.
Do not take RCIN SUSPENSION if you are allergic to Rifampicin and/or any other constituents present in the medicine.

Others

RCIN SUSPENSION is not recommended for use if you:

Have yellowish tinge to eyes and skin which may be indicative of jaundice 

Before taking RCIN SUSPENSION, inform your doctor if you:

Have diabetes (elevated level of sugar in blood)
Have peripheral neuropathy which is characterized by feeling of weakness and numbness in feet and hands
Are underweight and/or malnourished
Are diagnosed with a blood disorder called Porphyria characterized by the appearance of purple colored rash on skin.
Are prone to bleeding and/or bruising easily
Wear contact lens
Notice worsening and/or return of your initial symptoms of tuberculosis

Use in Pediatrics:
RCIN SUSPENSION must be taken in caution in children below 2 years of age. Consult your doctor before taking it as they can decide the correct and required dosage, frequency and strength of RCIN SUSPENSION based on age, disease condition and body weight of the child.

Use in Geriatrics:
RCIN SUSPENSION must be taken with caution in elderly patients (above the age of 65 years). Consult your doctor before taking RCIN SUSPENSION.

Before taking RCIN SUSPENSION, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicine:

Medicines used to manage indigestion such as antacids (Ex. aluminium hydroxide, magnesium carbonate)

Medicines used to thin the blood (Ex. clopidrogel, warfarrin)
Medicines used to lower cholesterol (Ex. atorvastatin, rosuvastatin)
Medicines for heart problems or to control your heartbeat (Ex. atenolol, bisprolol), lower the blood pressure (Ex. diuretics like eplerenone)
Medicines used to manage thought disorders (Ex. antipsychotics like haloperidol), reduce anxiety (Ex. hypnotics-lorazepam), to induce sleep (Ex. barbiturates-phenobarbital), manage depression (Ex. amitriptyline)
Medicines used to manage epilepsy (Ex. phenytoin), disease of motor neurons (Ex. riluzole)
Medicines used to manage various viral infections (Ex. indinavir, telaprevir, amprenavir, nelfinavir, atazanavir, lopinavir, neviparine, daclatasvir, simeprevir, sofosbuvir and telaprevir)
Medicines used to manage fungal diseases (Ex. ketoconazole, clotrimazole), bacterial infections (Ex. amoxicillin, cephalosporin), tapeworm infections (Ex. praziquantel)
Medicines used to lower the immune system response (Ex. ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus)
Medicines used to manage pneumonia (Ex. atovaquone)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took more of RCIN SUSPENSION, visit the nearby hospital or consult your doctor immediately. The symptoms of overdosage are nausea, vomiting, stomachache, itch and headache. The patient may also experience tiredness, sleepiness and dizziness, along with swelling of face and eyes, difficult breathing and fast, uneven heartbeat, heart attack and fits.

introduction:
Introduction About ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE

ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE is a combination of Isoniazid and Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antitubercular agents. It is used to manage tuberculosis and bacterial infection of membranes covering the brain, and spinal cord. It is also used to manage contagious disease of skin, nerves, mucous membrane, and other conditions in affected individuals.

ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients allergic to Isoniazid, and/or Rifampicin. Before taking ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you are scheduled for any upcoming surgery, and/or suffering from pre-existing diseases, liver problems (such as cirrhosis of liver)/kidney problems (such as renal insufficiency).

ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE should be used with caution during pregnancy and in women planning for pregnancy. It is also advised to be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it may pass through breast milk.

ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE should be used with caution in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) and is advised to be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65years and above) after consulting the doctor. 

The most common side effects of taking ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE are hypersensitivity reaction (associated with signs such as skin rash, red itchy welt, and/or shortness of breath), loss of vision/hearing, flu-like syndrome, and/or arthralgia (joint stiffness). Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsens.

ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE manages tuberculosis infection, where Rifampicin works by inactivating bacterial enzyme (RNA-polymerase) resulting in its destruction and Isoniazid works by managing the bacteria to form its own protective covering leading to its death thus managing tuberculosis in affected individuals.

Take ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE as advised by your physician. Swallow ANTICOX II 450/300MG CAPSULE with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of the medicine depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

name: MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE 10'S
introduction:
Introduction About MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE

MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE contains Rifampicin which belongs to the group of medicines called Antibacterial. It is used to manage bacterial infections such as tuberculosis (affects the lungs), legionnaires disease (lung inflammation), brucellosis (infection spreading from animal to person), leprosy (causes skin lesions and nerve damage) and serious staphylococcal infections.

It also manages the infections caused by Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitides (who are the carriers but do not show the symptoms), thereby managing and managing the onset of flu and meningitis. The doctor may ask you to take blood tests and liver function tests before starting management with MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE. MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you have yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice).

Before taking MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE, it is recommended to inform your doctor if you have liver, kidney problems, diabetes, are underweight or malnourished, have a rare blood problem (porphyria), bleeding or a tendency to bruise easily. Also, inform your doctor if symptoms of tuberculosis return or get worse, are wearing contact lenses, are vitamin K deficient or have hypoprothrombinemia (deficient clotting factor).

MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant and breastfeeding women. MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE should be used with caution in children under 2 years of age and in elderly patients above 65 years of age. The most common side effects seen are nausea, vomiting, chills, fever. Consult your doctor if symptoms do not improve.
uses: Infections caused by Haemophilus influenzae (causes flu) and Neisseria meningitides (causes meningitis)

How MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE Works

MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE works by managing protein synthesis and interferes with the enzymes present in the bacteria causing its death. This results in a reduction in the count of infection-causing bacteria, thereby managing bacterial infections.

Take MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Have yellowish tinge to eyes and skin which may be indicative of jaundice

Before taking MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you:

Are diagnosed with diabetes (elevated level of sugar in blood)
Are underweight and/or malnourished
Are diagnosed with a blood disorder called Porphyria characterized by the appearance of purple colored rash on skin
Are prone to bleeding and/or bruising
Wear contact lenses
Have deficiency of Vitamin K
If symptoms of tuberculosis return or get worse
Have hypoprothrombinemia (deficient clotting factor)

Use in Pediatrics:
MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE must be taken in caution in children below 2 years of age. Consult your doctor before taking it as they can decide the correct and required dosage, frequency and strength of MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE based on age, disease condition and body weight of the child.

Use in Geriatrics:
MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE must be taken in caution in elderly patients (above the age of 65 years). Consult your doctor before taking MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE.
interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug Interactions:

Before taking MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicine:

Medicines used to manage HIV infection (Ex. saquinavir, ritonavir)
Medicines used to manage indigestion such as antacids (Ex. aluminium hydroxide, magnesium carbonate)
Other medicines used to manage tuberculosis (Ex. P-Aminosalicylic Acid)
Medicines used to thin the blood (Ex. clopidrogel, warfarrin)
Medicines used to lower cholesterol (Ex. atorvastatin, rosuvastatin)
Medicines for heart problems or to control your heartbeat (Ex. atenolol, bisprolol), lower the blood pressure (Ex. diuretics like eplerenone)
Medicines used to manage thought disorders (Ex. antipsychotics like haloperidol), reduce anxiety (Ex. hypnotics-lorazepam), to induce sleep (Ex. barbiturates-phenobarbital), manage depression (Ex. amitriptyline)
Medicines used to manage epilepsy (Ex. phenytoin), disease of motor neurons (Ex. riluzole)
Medicines used to manage various viral infections (Ex. indinavir, telaprevir, amprenavir, nelfinavir, atazanavir, lopinavir, neviparine, daclatasvir, simeprevir, sofosbuvir and telaprevir)
Medicines used to manage fungal diseases (Ex. ketoconazole, clotrimazole), bacterial infections (Ex. amoxicillin, cephalosporin), tapeworm infections (Ex. praziquantel)
Medicines used to lower the immune system response (Ex. ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus)
Medicines used to manage pneumonia (Ex. atovaquone)
Medicines used for contraception (Ex. estrogen, progestogens)
Medicines used to manage cancer (Ex. imatinib, irinotecan, ethinyloestradiol, levonorgestrel or dydrogesterone), for breast cancer or endometriosis (Ex. tamoxifen, gestrinone, toremifene)
Medicines used to manage thyroid gland problems (Ex. levothyroxine)
Medicines used to manage gout and other pains (Ex. aspirin, etoricoxib, codeine, morphine, fentanyl, pethidine, etoricoxib, aspirin and indomethacin)
Medicines used to manage inflammation in the body such as corticosteroids (Ex. hydrocortisone, betamethasone and prednisolone)
Medicines used during withdrawal from heroin (Ex. methadone)
Medicines used to manage diabetes (Ex. metformin)
Medicines used before surgery to relax the mind and body (Ex. halothane)
Medicines used for nausea (Ex. ondansetron, aprepitant)
Medicines used for malaria (Ex. quinine)
Medicines used to manage difficulty breathing and wheezing sound (Ex. theophylline)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took too much of MONTOMYCIN 450MG CAPSULE, visit the nearby hospital or consult your doctor immediately. Signs and symptoms of overdosage are feeling sick (nausea) along with vomiting and pain in abdomen, increased itch (pruritus), headache and increased lethargy, feeling of drowsiness, swelling of the face, eyes or eyelids, fast or uneven heartbeat, dizziness, fits and heart attack.
